title: Wheel metadata omits the documented CLI and prompt assets

evidence.quote: sends each window to an LLM with a structured PT-BR prompt

reasoning: The build metadata declares a Hatch wheel but only packages the two import packages. The documented CLI is the top-level main.py script, and extraction depends on prompt files outside those packages. A wheel built from this metadata will not expose the documented command path or ship the prompt assets, so installed consumers can get a package that cannot run the documented pipeline.
recommendation: Either make the project explicitly source-checkout-only, or package the CLI and assets: add a console script, include the top-level CLI module or move it into a package, and include prompts/*.txt as package data or force-included wheel files.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and the README test commands exercise the source tree rather than building and installing the wheel.
suggestedRegressionTest: Build the wheel in CI, install it into a temporary environment, run the installed CLI help command, and assert the extraction, metadata, and verify prompt files are accessible without the repository root.
minimumFixScope: pyproject.toml wheel/script metadata plus lock/build verification; possibly a small package-layout move if main.py is moved under an import package.
